name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "Agent-generated hypothesis: R28 sits in the Btk PH-domain inositol-phosphate pocket (UniProt binding site for Ins(1,3,4,5)P4), and the Arg-to-His change removes the positive charge and H-bond geometry needed to bind the phosphate head group of Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 or phosphoinositides, so PH-domain membrane recruitment and BTK activation are lost.", "mechanism_class": "ligand_binding", "supports": ["E1", "E10", "E18", "E3", "E4", "E14"], "would_refute": "Ligand-bound experimental structures (e.g. 1B55 with 4IP) show residue 28 with no side-chain or backbone contact to the inositol phosphate, and a homology model or docked R28H structure keeps the ligand pose and contact energy within the wild-type range (no loss of contact or interaction energy at position 28).", "starting_rank": 1, "rank_rationale": "Ranked first because the only R28-specific functional study (E1, MD with MM/PBSA) classifies R28C/H as altering the ligand-binding site rather than folding, and UniProt (E10) lists residue 28 as an experimentally supported Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 binding site with a ligand-bound structure (E18). Missing: no wet-lab binding measurement for R28H (G1), so this rests on computation and annotation."}
